executive_summary:
**UPDATE 2026-10-19:** The CME × Silicon Data H100 and B200 Rental Index futures **listed and began trading on NYMEX on 2026-10-05** — compute futures are live, no longer pending. First-week volume/OI not yet publicly reported (the validation metric to watch). Architect expanded the AI Exchange with **Liquid Inference**, a real-time exchange for AI inference (2026-10-07, pending regulatory review). The CFTC's Request for Comment on compute derivatives closes **2026-10-20** — an approval/next-step window opens now. ICE/Ornn futures remain announced but unlaunched.

GPU-hour futures are now a listed asset class: CME × Silicon Data slated H100/B200 futures for **2026-10-05 pending CFTC approval** (now live, see update above), Architect already trades compute futures outside the US, and Nodal × Compute Desk entered 2026-09-03. Four price indexes (Silicon Data, Ornn, Compute Desk, SemiAnalysis) settle the same market and **diverged ~$1/hr** on identical accelerators — settlement-index choice materially changes hedge outcomes. Beneath them, 20+ spot marketplaces span a ~25× price range ($0.29–$8+/hr), the fragmentation that indexes and derivatives exist to fix.

**Conviction:** real and verified, but pre-liquidity. **Validation metric:** first-month open interest on whichever contract launches first. **Key risk:** CFTC timing plus index divergence undermining settlement trust.

This is the 1980s oil-futures moment for compute: spot markets existed first, then benchmarks, then listed price risk.

digests.title: Compute Trading Intel — Week of 2026-10-19
digests.body:
— Executive summary
The market's core validation event landed: CME × Silicon Data's H100 and B200 Rental Index futures listed on NYMEX on 2026-10-05, converting compute from "pending" to a listed asset class. First-week volume/open-interest figures are not yet publicly confirmed — that remains the key liquidity metric to track. Architect expanded its AI Exchange stack with "Liquid Inference," a real-time exchange for AI inference (announced 2026-10-07, pending regulatory review), extending tradability from GPU rentals to inference itself. On the regulatory layer, the CFTC's Request for Comment on compute derivatives closes 2026-10-20, so an outcome window opens this week. ICE/Ornn compute futures remain announced but unlaunched; no material spot-marketplace moves or new GPU-collateral credit deals surfaced this week.
